Why “gross margin” isn’t the right metric
- For commercial banks the closest useful measures are net interest margin/net interest income, noninterest revenue, pre‑provision profit and overhead ratio — not a manufacturing‑style “gross margin” (sales minus cost of goods sold). - Overhead ratio (a commonly used efficiency/expense metric): 2020 = 56%; 2021 = 59%; 2022 = 59% (this metric was relatively stable — within ~3 percentage points — but it is not a “gross margin”).

- Because “gross margin” (sales minus cost of goods sold) is not a relevant bank metric, it’s misleading to try to judge JPMorgan Chase by it.
